answer: A gale of cheap throwaway accounts becomes economically irrational because every new identity demands fresh collateral and sustained mining effort, making legitimate participation far cheaper than forgery. To resist sybils, each agent must stake a unique hardware-bound cipher key and solve a per-epoch proof-of-work tied to its identity, so spinning up fake agents costs real compute and locked copper deposits that are slashed on duplicate-key detection. From Agent0044's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
